### Sensitivity: Rd sub-model with fish biomass

This refits the metabolism block with log total fish biomass added to the Rd equation. The annual block is unaffected. Because Rd and Pmax residuals are correlated, the comparison uses the joint Rd–Pmax likelihood.

```{r sem-season-fish-diagnostics}
#| label: sem-season-fish-diagnostics

# Evidence cited inline in the justification text below: collinearity of
# fish with coral cover, and the fish share of measured Rd

rd_rows <- semdata_season |> filter(sub_rd)

fish_rd_cor <- cor(rd_rows$logcoral_z, rd_rows$logfish)
n_rd_years  <- n_distinct(rd_rows$year_f)

fish_rd_pct <- YearSeason_Averages |>
  filter(!is.na(Rd)) |>
  summarise(
    min_pct    = min(100 * Rfish_field_mmolO2_m2_h / Rd),
    median_pct = median(100 * Rfish_field_mmolO2_m2_h / Rd),
    max_pct    = max(100 * Rfish_field_mmolO2_m2_h / Rd)
  )

fish_rd_cor
fish_rd_pct
```

```{r sem-season-fish}
#| label: sem-season-model-fish
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["sem-season-preparation", "sem-season-metab-model"]

bf_logrd_s_fish <- bf(logrd ~ 1 + logcoral_z + logfleshy_z + temperature + summer +
                        logfish + (1 | p | year_f), family = gaussian())

brms_sem_season_metab_fish <- brm(
  bf_logrd_s_fish + bf_logpmax_s + set_rescor(TRUE),
  data = semdata_metab,
  chains = 3,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  seed = 6081,
  sample_prior = "no",
  prior = metab_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)
```

```{r sem-season-fish-compare}
#| label: sem-season-fish-comparison

# Joint Rd-Pmax likelihood of the metabolism block; the annual block is
# identical across models
loo_metab_main <- loo_block(brms_sem_season_metab)
loo_metab_fish <- loo_block(brms_sem_season_metab_fish)
fish_loo_cmp <- loo::loo_compare(list(main_no_fish = loo_metab_main,
                                      with_fish    = loo_metab_fish))
fish_loo_cmp

# Coefficient as "est (95% CI lo, hi)" plus a flag for CI excluding zero
coef_ci <- function(m, par) {
  fe <- fixef(m)[par, ]
  list(
    text     = sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s, %s)", fmt(fe[["Estimate"]]),
                       fmt(fe[["Q2.5"]]), fmt(fe[["Q97.5"]])),
    excludes0 = sign(fe[["Q2.5"]]) == sign(fe[["Q97.5"]])
  )
}

coral_rd_main <- coef_ci(brms_sem_season_metab, "logrd_logcoral_z")
coral_rd_fish <- coef_ci(brms_sem_season_metab_fish, "logrd_logcoral_z")
fish_rd_fish  <- coef_ci(brms_sem_season_metab_fish, "logrd_logfish")

# Absolute ELPD difference; "meaningful" if it exceeds 2 SE
fish_elpd_diff <- abs(fish_loo_cmp[2, "elpd_diff"])
fish_elpd_se   <- fish_loo_cmp[2, "se_diff"]
fish_loo_meaningful <- fish_elpd_diff > 2 * fish_elpd_se

tibble(
  Model    = c("Main (no fish)", "With fish"),
  coral_Rd = c(coral_rd_main$text, coral_rd_fish$text),
  R2_Rd    = sapply(list(brms_sem_season_metab, brms_sem_season_metab_fish),
                    \(m) bayes_r2_resp("logrd", fit = m))
)
```

Total fish biomass was left out of the respiration sub-model for three reasons. First, fish respiration cannot plausibly drive community Rd at this site: field-based estimates of fish respiration were `r fmt(fish_rd_pct$min_pct, 1)`–`r fmt(fish_rd_pct$max_pct, 1)`% of measured Rd (median `r fmt(fish_rd_pct$median_pct, 1)`%). Second, log fish biomass and log coral cover were correlated across the seasonal observations (r = `r fmt(fish_rd_cor)`), because both followed the same multi-decadal trend as coral declined and fish biomass increased. With only `r n_rd_years` independent years, including both predictors split one shared signal between them. The coral cover coefficient was `r coral_rd_main$text` without fish and `r coral_rd_fish$text` with fish`r if (coral_rd_main$excludes0 && !coral_rd_fish$excludes0) ", so its credible interval widened to include zero" else ""`. Fish took a coefficient of `r fish_rd_fish$text`, which is implausibly large for a sub-1% metabolic contribution. Third, adding fish `r if (fish_loo_meaningful) "changed" else "did not meaningfully change"` out-of-sample prediction of Rd: the absolute difference in PSIS-LOO expected log predictive density for the joint Rd–Pmax likelihood was `r fmt(fish_elpd_diff, 1)` ± `r fmt(fish_elpd_se, 1)` (SE).

## Downstream effects of coral loss: structural causal models

The seasonal SEM estimates every path at once. In a single joint model, each coefficient is conditioned on everything else in its equation, so some coefficients are direct effects, some are total effects, and some may be biased because they condition on a mediator or a collider (the "Table 2 fallacy"). Here we follow the structural causal model (SCM) workflow of Arif et al. (2022, *Ecosphere* 13:e3956) and Arif & MacNeil (2023, *Ecological Monographs* e1554) to estimate the causal effects of coral cover on the rest of the system:

1. Encode the assumed causal structure as a directed acyclic graph (DAG), including drivers we do not treat as outcomes.
2. Check the DAG against the data using the conditional independencies it implies.
3. For each effect of interest, use the backdoor criterion (`dagitty::adjustmentSets()`) to find a minimal set of covariates that blocks all non-causal paths between coral cover and the outcome, without conditioning on mediators or colliders.
4. Fit one Bayesian regression per effect with exactly that adjustment set, and interpret only the coral coefficient.

The question is the downstream impact of coral loss, so coral cover is the exposure in every model. The outcomes are fleshy algae cover, herbivore, corallivore and total fish biomass, N content, Rd and Pmax. Effects are estimated as **total effects** (everything that follows from a change in coral cover, including algal replacement of lost coral) and, for metabolism, also as **direct effects** (holding fleshy algae and the other mediators constant, i.e. coral replaced by "other" substrate).

### Causal DAG

The initial DAG differs from the SEM in one important way: coral cover is treated as a cause of same-year fleshy algae cover (space released by coral mortality is colonised by algae), while algae affect coral only with a lag (previous-year algae suppress coral recovery). Temperature can trigger disturbance (bleaching), and disturbance can act on metabolism directly (bleached coral photosynthesises less before it dies; storms scour the benthos). Fish affect N content through excretion and contribute to Rd. Rd and Pmax share unmeasured drivers (dashed bidirected arc). Season affects metabolism only, so it is a precision covariate rather than a confounder.

The revised DAG adds arrows after testing the initial DAG against the data (next section): Year is linked to every annual variable as a proxy for slow, unmeasured drivers (fishing, land-based nutrients, regional change, the clustering of COTS and bleaching disturbances in time); herbivore and corallivore biomass are components of total fish biomass; and previous-year herbivores facilitate coral (grazing frees space for coral recruits).

```{r coral-scm-dag}
#| label: fig-coral-scm-dag
#| fig-cap: "Causal DAGs for the downstream effects of coral cover. Red = exposure; blue = downstream outcomes; grey = other variables. Green arrows were added to the initial DAG after testing its implied independencies. The dashed arc is a residual correlation (shared unmeasured causes) between Rd and Pmax."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 14

# dagitty is called with :: because its edges() masks igraph::edges()
coral_dag_text <- 'dag {
  Year -> Temp
  Temp -> Dist
  Temp -> Coral ; Temp -> Fleshy ; Temp -> Rd ; Temp -> Pmax
  Dist -> Coral ; Dist -> Fleshy ; Dist -> Rd ; Dist -> Pmax
  CoralLag -> Coral ; CoralLag -> FleshyLag ; FleshyLag -> Fleshy ; FleshyLag -> Coral
  CoralLag -> CorallivLag ; FleshyLag -> HerbLag
  CorallivLag -> Coral ; CorallivLag -> Coralliv
  HerbLag -> Fleshy ; HerbLag -> Herb
  Coral -> Fleshy
  Coral -> Coralliv ; Coral -> Herb ; Fleshy -> Herb
  Coral -> Fish ; Fleshy -> Fish
  Coral -> N ; Fleshy -> N ; Fish -> N
  Coral -> Rd ; Fleshy -> Rd ; Fish -> Rd
  Coral -> Pmax ; Fleshy -> Pmax ; N -> Pmax
  Season -> Rd ; Season -> Pmax
  Rd <-> Pmax
}'
coral_dag <- dagitty::dagitty(coral_dag_text)

# Revised after the local tests: Year as a proxy for slow unmeasured drivers
# of every annual variable (lags included), fish groups as components of
# total fish, and herbivore facilitation of coral
coral_dag_revised <- dagitty::dagitty(sub(
  "Year -> Temp",
  paste("Year -> Temp ; Year -> Dist ; Year -> Coral ; Year -> Fleshy ;",
        "Year -> Fish ; Year -> Herb ; Year -> Coralliv ; Year -> N ;",
        "Year -> CoralLag ; Year -> FleshyLag ; Year -> HerbLag ; Year -> CorallivLag ;",
        "Herb -> Fish ; Coralliv -> Fish ; HerbLag -> Coral"),
  coral_dag_text, fixed = TRUE
))

# DAG node -> modelled variable
coral_node_vars <- c(
  Year = "Year", Temp = "temperature", Dist = "Disturbance",
  CoralLag = "lr_coral_lag1", FleshyLag = "lr_fleshy_lag1",
  HerbLag = "logherbs_lag1", CorallivLag = "logcoralliv_lag1",
  Coral = "logcoral", Fleshy = "logfleshy", Herb = "logherbs",
  Coralliv = "logcoralliv", Fish = "logfish", N = "logN",
  Rd = "logrd", Pmax = "logpmax", Season = "summer"
)
coral_node_labels <- c(
  Year = "Year", Temp = "Max\ntemperature", Dist = "Disturbance",
  CoralLag = "Coral\n(t\u22121)", FleshyLag = "Fleshy algae\n(t\u22121)",
  HerbLag = "Herbivores\n(t\u22121)", CorallivLag = "Corallivores\n(t\u22121)",
  Coral = "Coral\ncover", Fleshy = "Fleshy algae\ncover", Herb = "Herbivore\nbiomass",
  Coralliv = "Corallivore\nbiomass", Fish = "Total fish\nbiomass", N = "N content",
  Rd = "Rd", Pmax = "Pmax", Season = "Season"
)
coral_outcomes <- c("Fleshy", "Herb", "Coralliv", "Fish", "N", "Rd", "Pmax")
coral_outcome_labels <- c(
  Fleshy = "Fleshy algae cover", Herb = "Herbivore biomass",
  Coralliv = "Corallivore biomass", Fish = "Total fish biomass",
  N = "N content", Rd = "Ecosystem Rd", Pmax = "Ecosystem Pmax"
)

coral_dag_coords <- tribble(
  ~name,          ~x,  ~y,
  "Year",          0,   7,
  "Temp",          2,   7,
  "Dist",          4,   7,
  "CoralLag",      0,   4.5,
  "CorallivLag",   2,   5.5,
  "FleshyLag",     0,   1.5,
  "HerbLag",       2,   0,
  "Coral",         4,   4.5,
  "Fleshy",        4,   1.5,
  "Coralliv",      6.5, 5.5,
  "Fish",          6.5, 3,
  "Herb",          6.5, 0,
  "N",             8.5, 1.5,
  "Rd",           10.5, 4.5,
  "Pmax",         10.5, 1.5,
  "Season",       12.5, 3
)

# Edge list with ends trimmed to an elliptical box around each node label;
# `added` flags edges that are not in the initial DAG
dag_edge_data <- function(dag, coords = coral_dag_coords, a = 0.65, b = 0.5,
                          base = coral_dag) {
  base_edges <- with(dagitty::edges(base), paste(v, w))
  as_tibble(dagitty::edges(dag)) |>
    transmute(from = as.character(v), to = as.character(w), type = as.character(e),
              added = !paste(from, to) %in% base_edges) |>
    left_join(select(coords, from = name, x, y), by = "from") |>
    left_join(select(coords, to = name, xend = x, yend = y), by = "to") |>
    mutate(
      len = sqrt((xend - x)^2 + (yend - y)^2),
      ux  = (xend - x) / len,
      uy  = (yend - y) / len,
      gap = 1 / sqrt((ux / a)^2 + (uy / b)^2),
      x = x + gap * ux, y = y + gap * uy,
      xend = xend - gap * ux, yend = yend - gap * uy
    )
}

coral_role_cols <- c("Exposure (coral cover)" = "#d6604d", "Outcome" = "#4393c3",
                     "Adjusted for" = "#fdb863", "Not adjusted" = "grey90")

dag_node_data <- function(outcomes, adjusted = character(0)) {
  coral_dag_coords |>
    mutate(
      label = coral_node_labels[name],
      role  = case_when(name == "Coral"     ~ "Exposure (coral cover)",
                        name %in% outcomes  ~ "Outcome",
                        name %in% adjusted  ~ "Adjusted for",
                        TRUE                ~ "Not adjusted"),
      role  = factor(role, names(coral_role_cols))
    )
}

plot_coral_dag <- function(nodes, edges, label_size = 3.5) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = filter(edges, type == "->"),
                 aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, colour = added),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                 linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_curve(data = filter(edges, type == "<->"),
               aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend), curvature = -0.4,
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed", ends = "both")) +
    geom_label(data = nodes, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fill = role),
               size = label_size, lineheight = 0.85, label.size = 0.2,
               key_glyph = "rect") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = coral_role_cols, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey45", `TRUE` = "#1b7837"),
                        labels = c(`FALSE` = "Initial DAG", `TRUE` = "Added after testing"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
          text = element_text(size = 13))
}

(plot_coral_dag(dag_node_data(coral_outcomes), dag_edge_data(coral_dag)) +
    ggtitle("a) Initial DAG") + theme(legend.position = "none")) /
  (plot_coral_dag(dag_node_data(coral_outcomes), dag_edge_data(coral_dag_revised)) +
     ggtitle("b) Revised DAG"))
ggsave(here("Output", "fig_scm_dag.pdf"), width = 12, height = 14)
```

### Testable implications of the DAG

Every missing arrow in a DAG is an assumption, and many of them imply that two variables are independent once some others are held fixed. These implications can be checked against the annual data (Rd, Pmax and Season are seasonal, so they are left out here). Each test is a partial correlation; values far from zero suggest a missing arrow. With 95% intervals, about 5% of tests should exclude zero by chance even if the DAG is right. With about 19 years the tests also have little power, so passing is a screen for gross misspecification rather than a confirmation of the DAG.

```{r coral-scm-data}
#| label: coral-scm-data

# Rebuilt from the source tables rather than semdata_season, whose NAs are
# replaced by 0 placeholders for the brms subset() machinery
coral_scm_log <- YearSeason_Averages |>
  left_join(annual_lags, by = "Year") |>
  arrange(Year, Season) |>
  transmute(
    Year, Season, Disturbance,
    annual_row       = !duplicated(Year),
    seasonal_row     = !is.na(Season),
    year_f           = factor(Year),
    summer           = case_when(Season == "Summer" ~ 0.5,
                                 Season == "Winter" ~ -0.5,
                                 TRUE ~ 0),
    temperature      = Max_temp,
    lr_coral_lag1, lr_fleshy_lag1,
    logherbs_lag1    = log(Herbivores_lag1),
    logcoralliv_lag1 = log(Corallivore_lag1),
    logcoral         = log(mean_coral / 100),
    logfleshy        = log(mean_fleshy / 100),
    logherbs         = log(Herbivores),
    logcoralliv      = log(Corallivore),
    logfish          = log(fish_biomass_g_m2),
    logN             = log(N_percent),
    logrd            = log(Rd),
    logpmax          = log(Pmax)
  )

# Annual variables are standardised over one row per year, Rd and Pmax over
# the seasonal rows; the means and SDs are kept to back-transform effects
scm_annual_vars   <- c("Year", "temperature", "lr_coral_lag1", "lr_fleshy_lag1",
                       "logherbs_lag1", "logcoralliv_lag1", "logcoral", "logfleshy",
                       "logherbs", "logcoralliv", "logfish", "logN")
scm_seasonal_vars <- c("logrd", "logpmax")

coral_scm_scale <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(scm_annual_vars, \(v) {
    x <- coral_scm_log[[v]][coral_scm_log$annual_row]
    tibble(var = v, mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  }),
  map_dfr(scm_seasonal_vars, \(v) {
    x <- coral_scm_log[[v]][coral_scm_log$seasonal_row]
    tibble(var = v, mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
)

coral_scm_data <- coral_scm_log |>
  mutate(across(all_of(scm_annual_vars), \(x) scale_on(x, annual_row)),
         across(all_of(scm_seasonal_vars), \(x) scale_on(x, seasonal_row)))

# Years available to the annual models
coral_scm_data |>
  filter(annual_row) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(scm_annual_vars), \(x) sum(!is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_years")
```

```{r coral-scm-local-tests}
#| label: fig-coral-scm-local-tests
#| fig-cap: "Conditional independencies implied by each DAG among the annual variables. Points are partial correlations with 95% intervals; the DAG predicts zero for every row. Red = interval excludes zero. Only failed tests are labelled; 'A _||_ B | C' reads 'A is independent of B given C'."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

annual_nodes <- setdiff(names(coral_node_vars), c("Rd", "Pmax", "Season"))

coral_lt_data <- coral_scm_data |>
  filter(annual_row) |>
  select(all_of(unname(coral_node_vars[annual_nodes]))) |>
  set_names(annual_nodes) |>
  drop_na()

run_local_tests <- function(dag) {
  cis <- dagitty::impliedConditionalIndependencies(dag) |>
    keep(\(ci) all(c(ci$X, ci$Y, ci$Z) %in% annual_nodes))
  dagitty::localTests(dag, data = coral_lt_data, type = "cis", tests = cis,
                      abbreviate.names = FALSE) |>
    as_tibble(rownames = "test") |>
    rename(lo = `2.5%`, hi = `97.5%`) |>
    mutate(flag = sign(lo) == sign(hi))
}

coral_local_tests <- bind_rows(
  `a) Initial DAG` = run_local_tests(coral_dag),
  `b) Revised DAG` = run_local_tests(coral_dag_revised),
  .id = "dag"
)

coral_lt_summary <- coral_local_tests |>
  group_by(dag) |>
  summarise(n_tests = n(), n_fail = sum(flag), expected = 0.05 * n())
coral_lt_summary

coral_local_tests |>
  group_by(dag) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(estimate, ties.method = "first")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = rank, colour = flag)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), size = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = \(d) filter(d, flag),
            aes(x = if_else(estimate > 0, lo, hi), label = test,
                hjust = if_else(estimate > 0, 1.03, -0.03)),
            size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey60", `TRUE` = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1.6, 1.6), breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ dag, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Partial correlation", y = "Implied independence (ranked)") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(size = 13))
```

Under the initial DAG, `r coral_lt_summary$n_fail[1]` of `r coral_lt_summary$n_tests[1]` implied independencies failed (about `r round(coral_lt_summary$expected[1])` expected by chance). Almost all of the failures involved Year: coral, fleshy algae, fish, herbivores, corallivores, N content and disturbance all trend through time in ways that temperature alone does not explain. The largest single failure was total fish biomass and herbivore biomass being independent given cover, which cannot hold because herbivores are part of total fish biomass. Previous-year herbivores were also associated with coral beyond what previous-year algae explained. After adding these arrows, `r coral_lt_summary$n_fail[2]` of `r coral_lt_summary$n_tests[2]` tests failed, in line with chance. The remaining failures (a residual association between herbivore and corallivore biomass, and between total fish and previous-year algae) point to shared drivers of fish groups that the DAG does not represent; neither changes the adjustment sets for coral effects below. All effects below are estimated under the revised DAG, with the initial DAG shown for comparison.

### Adjustment sets from the backdoor criterion

For each effect, `adjustmentSets()` returns the minimal sets of covariates that close every backdoor path from coral cover to the outcome. When more than one minimal set exists the smallest is used. Total effects must not adjust for mediators (e.g. fleshy algae for the effect on Pmax), while direct effects must adjust for them. Season is added to the metabolism models as a precision covariate: it is not on any backdoor path, but it explains outcome variance.

```{r coral-scm-adjustment-sets}
#| label: coral-scm-adjustment-sets

coral_dags <- list("Revised DAG" = coral_dag_revised, "Initial DAG" = coral_dag)

pick_adjustment <- function(dag, outcome, effect) {
  sets <- dagitty::adjustmentSets(dag, exposure = "Coral", outcome = outcome,
                                  effect = effect)
  if (length(sets) == 0) stop("Coral -> ", outcome, " (", effect, ") is not identifiable")
  sort(sets[[which.min(lengths(sets))]])
}

coral_estimands <- bind_rows(
  tibble(dag = "Revised DAG", outcome = coral_outcomes, effect = "total"),
  tibble(dag = "Revised DAG", outcome = c("Rd", "Pmax"), effect = "direct"),
  tibble(dag = "Initial DAG", outcome = coral_outcomes, effect = "total")
) |>
  mutate(
    adjust    = pmap(list(dag, outcome, effect),
                     \(d, o, e) pick_adjustment(coral_dags[[d]], o, e)),
    precision = map(outcome, \(o) if (o %in% c("Rd", "Pmax")) "Season" else character(0)),
    estimand  = glue("{coral_outcome_labels[outcome]} ({effect})")
  )

coral_estimands |>
  transmute(
    DAG = dag, Outcome = coral_outcome_labels[outcome], Effect = effect,
    `Adjustment set` = map_chr(adjust, \(a) paste(gsub("\n", " ", coral_node_labels[a]),
                                                  collapse = ", ")),
    `Precision covariates` = map_chr(precision, \(p) paste(p, collapse = ", "))
  ) |>
  kbl() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
```

```{r coral-scm-adjustment-dags}
#| label: fig-coral-scm-adjustment-dags
#| fig-cap: "Adjustment sets for each effect of coral cover under the revised DAG. Red = exposure, blue = outcome, orange = covariates adjusted for. Every other variable is left out of that model."
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 13

coral_main_estimands <- filter(coral_estimands, dag == "Revised DAG")

adj_nodes <- coral_main_estimands |>
  mutate(nodes = map2(outcome, adjust, \(o, a) dag_node_data(o, a))) |>
  select(estimand, nodes) |>
  unnest(nodes)
# Edge colour is not needed here, so every edge is drawn as "initial"
adj_edges <- tidyr::crossing(estimand = coral_main_estimands$estimand,
                             dag_edge_data(coral_dag_revised)) |>
  mutate(added = FALSE)

plot_coral_dag(adj_nodes, adj_edges, label_size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(estimand, coral_main_estimands$estimand), ncol = 3) +
  guides(colour = "none") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold",
                                  margin = margin(b = 4)))
```

### One model per causal effect

Each effect gets its own `brm()` model with only coral cover, the adjustment set and any precision covariates. Annual outcomes are fit to one row per year. Rd and Pmax are fit to the seasonal rows with a year random intercept, because the annual predictors are repeated across the two seasons. All continuous variables are standardised (log scale for cover, biomass, N and metabolism), so the coral coefficient is the change in SD of the log outcome per SD of log coral cover. Priors are weakly informative, normal(0, 1) on coefficients.

```{r coral-scm-fits}
#| label: coral-scm-fits
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["coral-scm-data", "coral-scm-adjustment-sets"]

fit_coral_effect <- function(outcome, adjust, precision) {
  resp     <- coral_node_vars[[outcome]]
  preds    <- unname(coral_node_vars[c("Coral", adjust, precision)])
  seasonal <- outcome %in% c("Rd", "Pmax")

  dat <- coral_scm_data |>
    filter(if (seasonal) seasonal_row else annual_row) |>
    drop_na(all_of(c(resp, preds)))

  rhs <- paste(c(preds, if (seasonal) "(1 | year_f)"), collapse = " + ")
  pri <- prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b") +
    prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept") +
    prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma")
  if (seasonal) pri <- pri + prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "sd")

  brm(as.formula(paste(resp, "~", rhs)), data = dat, family = gaussian(),
      prior = pri, chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 2738,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), silent = 2, refresh = 0)
}

coral_scm_fits <- coral_estimands |>
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(outcome, adjust, precision), fit_coral_effect))
```

```{r coral-scm-diagnostics}
#| label: coral-scm-diagnostics

# Convergence and sample size for every model
coral_scm_fits |>
  transmute(
    estimand, dag,
    n        = map_int(fit, nobs),
    max_rhat = map_dbl(fit, \(f) max(brms::rhat(f), na.rm = TRUE)),
    min_ess  = map_dbl(fit, \(f) min(posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_df(f),
                                                                "ess_bulk")$ess_bulk,
                                    na.rm = TRUE)),
    divergent = map_int(fit, \(f) sum(nuts_params(f) |>
                                        filter(Parameter == "divergent__") |>
                                        pull(Value)))
  )
```

### Visualising and interpreting the causal effects

The coral coefficient is converted to an interpretable quantity: the expected percentage change in each outcome if coral cover were halved, with all other causes of the outcome held at their observed values. Because both coral cover and the outcomes are on the log scale, this is

$$
\%\Delta Y = 100\left[\exp\left(\beta \, \frac{\mathrm{SD}_{\log Y}}{\mathrm{SD}_{\log \mathrm{coral}}}\, \log 0.5\right) - 1\right]
$$

For the **total effect**, the change includes everything that follows from losing coral, including any fleshy algae that grow into the space. The **direct effect** on metabolism holds fleshy algae (and fish or N) at their observed values, so it describes coral being replaced by other substrate (sand, rubble, crustose coralline algae). The difference between the two is the part of the coral effect that runs through algal replacement and the consumer/nutrient pathway.

```{r coral-scm-effects}
#| label: coral-scm-effects

coral_sd <- coral_scm_scale$sd[coral_scm_scale$var == "logcoral"]

coral_effect_draws <- coral_scm_fits |>
  mutate(
    sd_out = map_dbl(outcome, \(o) coral_scm_scale$sd[coral_scm_scale$var == coral_node_vars[[o]]]),
    draws  = map(fit, \(f) as_draws_df(f)$b_logcoral)
  ) |>
  select(dag, outcome, effect, estimand, sd_out, draws) |>
  unnest(draws) |>
  rename(beta = draws) |>
  mutate(
    pct_halving   = 100 * (exp(beta * sd_out / coral_sd * log(0.5)) - 1),
    outcome_label = factor(coral_outcome_labels[outcome], rev(coral_outcome_labels)),
    effect        = factor(str_to_sentence(effect), c("Total", "Direct"))
  )

coral_effect_summary <- coral_effect_draws |>
  group_by(dag, outcome, outcome_label, effect) |>
  summarise(
    beta_med  = median(beta),
    beta_lo   = quantile(beta, 0.025),
    beta_hi   = quantile(beta, 0.975),
    pct_med   = median(pct_halving),
    pct_lo    = quantile(pct_halving, 0.025),
    pct_hi    = quantile(pct_halving, 0.975),
    p_decline = mean(pct_halving < 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

coral_effect_summary |>
  arrange(dag, desc(outcome_label), effect) |>
  transmute(
    DAG = dag, Outcome = as.character(outcome_label), Effect = effect,
    `Std. coefficient` = sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", fmt(beta_med), fmt(beta_lo), fmt(beta_hi)),
    `% change if coral halved` = sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", fmt(pct_med, 0), fmt(pct_lo, 0), fmt(pct_hi, 0)),
    `P(decline)` = round(p_decline, 2)
  ) |>
  kbl(align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "left")

# Inline helper: "median% (95% CI lo, hi); P(decline) = p"
scm_text <- function(o, e = "Total", d = "Revised DAG") {
  r <- filter(coral_effect_summary, outcome == o, effect == e, dag == d)
  sprintf("%s%% (95%% CI %s, %s); P(decline) = %s", fmt(r$pct_med, 0),
          fmt(r$pct_lo, 0), fmt(r$pct_hi, 0), fmt(r$p_decline))
}
```

```{r coral-scm-effects-plot}
#| label: fig-coral-scm-effects
#| fig-cap: "Causal effects of halving coral cover on downstream variables, each from its own DAG-informed model. Points are posterior medians, thick and thin bars 80% and 95% credible intervals. Total effects include algal replacement and all other downstream pathways; direct effects on metabolism hold fleshy algae, fish (Rd) and N (Pmax) constant. Left: revised DAG (adjusts for the long-term trend). Right: initial DAG, which ignores trend confounding, for comparison."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5

# Intervals are computed here and drawn with base geoms (stat_pointinterval
# is not compatible with every ggplot2/ggdist version combination)
coral_effect_intervals <- coral_effect_draws |>
  group_by(dag, outcome_label, effect) |>
  median_qi(pct_halving, .width = c(0.8, 0.95)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(dag = factor(dag, names(coral_dags)))

dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.6)
ggplot(coral_effect_intervals,
       aes(x = pct_halving, y = outcome_label, colour = effect, group = effect)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper, linewidth = factor(.width)),
                 position = dodge) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, .width == 0.95), size = 2.5, position = dodge) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`0.8` = 1.5, `0.95` = 0.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Total = "black", Direct = "#d6604d"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ dag) +
  labs(x = "% change in outcome if coral cover were halved", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 13))

ggsave(here("Output", "fig_scm_effects.pdf"), width = 11, height = 5.5)
```

```{r coral-scm-counterfactual}
#| label: fig-coral-scm-counterfactual
#| fig-cap: "Counterfactual Rd and Pmax across the observed range of coral cover, from the DAG-informed models. Lines are posterior medians with 90% credible bands, with all adjustment covariates at their means, no disturbance and an average season. Total = coral loss with the observed algal response; Direct = coral replaced by other substrate with fleshy algae, fish and N held constant. Points are the observed seasonal values."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

coral_grid <- tibble(coral_pct = seq(min(YearSeason_Averages$mean_coral, na.rm = TRUE),
                                     max(YearSeason_Averages$mean_coral, na.rm = TRUE),
                                     length.out = 50)) |>
  mutate(logcoral = (log(coral_pct / 100) - coral_scm_scale$mean[coral_scm_scale$var == "logcoral"]) /
           coral_sd)

coral_cf <- coral_scm_fits |>
  filter(dag == "Revised DAG", outcome %in% c("Rd", "Pmax")) |>
  mutate(pred = map(fit, \(f) {
    # Every predictor other than coral is held at 0: the mean of the
    # standardised covariates (mid-series for Year), no disturbance and the
    # average season
    other <- setdiff(all.vars(formula(f)$formula[[3]]), c("logcoral", "year_f"))
    nd <- coral_grid
    nd[other] <- 0
    add_epred_draws(nd, f, re_formula = NA, ndraws = 2000)
  })) |>
  select(outcome, effect, pred) |>
  unnest(pred) |>
  # Back-transform from the standardised log scale to natural units
  mutate(var = unname(coral_node_vars[outcome])) |>
  left_join(coral_scm_scale, by = "var") |>
  mutate(value  = exp(.epred * sd + mean),
         effect = factor(str_to_sentence(effect), c("Total", "Direct")))

coral_cf_obs <- YearSeason_Averages |>
  filter(!is.na(Season)) |>
  select(mean_coral, Rd, Pmax) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Rd, Pmax), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value")

coral_cf_summary <- coral_cf |>
  group_by(outcome, effect, coral_pct) |>
  median_qi(value, .width = 0.9) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(coral_cf_summary, aes(x = coral_pct, y = value)) +
  geom_point(data = coral_cf_obs, aes(x = mean_coral), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower, ymax = .upper, fill = effect), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = effect), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Total = "black", Direct = "#d6604d"), name = NULL,
                      aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(outcome, c("Rd", "Pmax")), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Coral cover (%)", y = "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 h\u207b\u00b9") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 13))
```

**How to read these results.** Each estimate answers one causal question under the stated DAG: "if coral cover were halved, by how much would this outcome change?" Only the coral coefficient of each model is interpretable; the adjustment covariates are there to block confounding, and their coefficients are not causal effects (they may themselves be confounded or partly mediated). Compared with the SEM, the total effects here do not hold fleshy algae constant: in the SEM, the coral→Pmax "total" effect (`r effect_text("coral_total")`, standardised) is conditional on fleshy algae and is therefore closer to the direct effect here. Under the revised DAG, halving coral cover changed Pmax by `r scm_text("Pmax")` in total and `r scm_text("Pmax", "Direct")` directly, and Rd by `r scm_text("Rd")` in total and `r scm_text("Rd", "Direct")` directly. For fleshy algae cover the total effect was `r scm_text("Fleshy")`; for N content `r scm_text("N")`; for corallivore biomass `r scm_text("Coralliv")`; for herbivore biomass `r scm_text("Herb")`; and for total fish biomass `r scm_text("Fish")`.

The gap between total and direct effects is the mediated part of the effect. A total effect that is clearly non-zero alongside a direct effect that overlaps zero (as for Rd here) means that most of the consequence of coral loss runs through what replaces the coral and through fish, rather than through the loss of coral tissue itself. Similar total and direct effects (as for Pmax) mean the mediators carry little of the effect. With this few years, a difference of this kind is suggestive rather than established: the total and direct intervals overlap, and the indirect effect is not estimated as a separate quantity. The right-hand panel shows how the conclusions would change under the initial DAG, which ignores the shared long-term trend.

**Caveats.** These are causal estimates only if the revised DAG is right, in particular if there are no unmeasured common causes of coral cover and an outcome beyond what a linear Year term captures. Coral declined almost monotonically from 2006 to about 2015 while fleshy algae and fish biomass increased. Adjusting for Year means the total effects are identified from year-to-year deviations around those trends, which is a much weaker source of information with about 19 years, so wide intervals are expected; it also means a genuine causal effect of coral that unfolds as a slow trend is partly absorbed by Year. For several outcomes the initial-DAG estimates are larger and more precise because they use the full trend, but the local tests indicate that they are confounded by it. The total-effect models carry six or more covariates on about 19 years, so they lean on the normal(0, 1) priors. Residual temporal autocorrelation is not modelled beyond the lagged covariates.

## Supplementary: coral dominance (single log-ratio) SEM

An earlier version of the seasonal SEM represented the benthos by a single log ratio of coral to fleshy algae cover (coral dominance). A log ratio is itself a compositional transformation, so this model is also unaffected by the shared total, but it cannot separate coral change from algal change. It is retained for comparison and as the basis for the disturbance-timing, AR(1) and recruitment analyses below. Its metabolism block uses coral dominance in place of log coral and log fleshy algae cover; all other settings match the main SEM.

```{r sem-season-cd-fit}
#| label: sem-season-cd-model
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["sem-season-preparation", "sem-season-metab-model"]

bf_coral_cd    <- bf(coraldom | subset(sub_coral) ~ 1 + coraldom_lag1 + temperature +
                       Disturbance + logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1 +
                       mi(logrec3, idx = obs_id), family = gaussian())
bf_coralliv_cd <- bf(logcoralliv | subset(sub_coralliv) ~ 1 + coraldom, family = gaussian())
bf_herbs_cd    <- bf(logherbs | subset(sub_herbs) ~ 1 + coraldom, family = gaussian())
bf_N_cd        <- bf(logN | subset(sub_N) ~ 1 + coraldom, family = gaussian())

annual_resps_cd  <- c("temperature", "coraldom", "logcoralliv", "logherbs", "logN")
annual_priors_cd <- c(
  do.call(c, lapply(annual_resps_cd, \(r) set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b", resp = r))),
  do.call(c, lapply(annual_resps_cd, \(r) set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept", resp = r))),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.25)", class = "sigma", resp = "temperature", lb = 0),
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept", resp = "logrec3")
)

brms_sem_season_annual_cd <- brm(
  bf_temp_s + bf_coral_cd + bf_rec_s + bf_coralliv_cd + bf_herbs_cd + bf_N_cd +
    set_rescor(FALSE),
  data = semdata_season, chains = 3, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000, seed = 6081,
  sample_prior = "no", prior = annual_priors_cd,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15), silent = 2, refresh = 0
)

brms_sem_season_metab_cd <- brm(
  bf(logrd ~ 1 + coraldom + temperature + summer + (1 | p | year_f), family = gaussian()) +
    bf(logpmax ~ 1 + coraldom + temperature + summer + logN + (1 | p | year_f),
       family = gaussian()) +
    set_rescor(TRUE),
  data = semdata_metab, chains = 3, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000, seed = 6081,
  sample_prior = "no", prior = metab_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15), silent = 2, refresh = 0
)
```

```{r sem-season-cd-compare}
#| label: sem-season-cd-comparison

fe_cd  <- season_fixef(brms_sem_season_annual_cd, brms_sem_season_metab_cd)
fe_dir <- season_fixef()

term_txt <- function(fe, term) {
  if (is.na(term)) return("\u2014")
  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", fe[term, "Estimate"], fe[term, "Q2.5"], fe[term, "Q97.5"])
}

# Matching paths in the two models (coral dominance vs Dirichlet / cover)
tribble(
  ~path,                                ~cd,                           ~dirichlet,
  "Temperature \u2192 coral",           "coraldom_temperature",        "mucoral_comp_temperature",
  "Temperature \u2192 fleshy algae",    NA,                            "mufleshy_comp_temperature",
  "Disturbance \u2192 coral",           "coraldom_Disturbance",        "mucoral_comp_Disturbance",
  "Disturbance \u2192 fleshy algae",    NA,                            "mufleshy_comp_Disturbance",
  "Recruitment (t\u22123) \u2192 coral", "coraldom_milogrec3idxEQobs_id", "mucoral_comp_milogrec3idxEQobs_id",
  "Herbivores (t\u22121) \u2192 benthos", "coraldom_logherbs_lag1",     "mufleshy_comp_logherbs_lag1",
  "Corallivores (t\u22121) \u2192 benthos", "coraldom_logcoralliv_lag1", "mucoral_comp_logcoralliv_lag1",
  "Benthos \u2192 herbivores",          "logherbs_coraldom",           "logherbs_logfleshy_z",
  "Benthos \u2192 corallivores",        "logcoralliv_coraldom",        "logcoralliv_logcoral_z",
  "Coral \u2192 N",                     "logN_coraldom",               "logN_logcoral_z",
  "Fleshy algae \u2192 N",              NA,                            "logN_logfleshy_z",
  "Coral \u2192 Rd",                    "logrd_coraldom",              "logrd_logcoral_z",
  "Fleshy algae \u2192 Rd",             NA,                            "logrd_logfleshy_z",
  "Coral \u2192 Pmax (direct)",         "logpmax_coraldom",            "logpmax_logcoral_z",
  "Fleshy algae \u2192 Pmax (direct)",  NA,                            "logpmax_logfleshy_z"
) |>
  mutate(
    `Coral dominance model` = map_chr(cd, \(t) term_txt(fe_cd, t)),
    `Dirichlet model`       = map_chr(dirichlet, \(t) term_txt(fe_dir, t))
  ) |>
  select(Path = path, `Coral dominance model`, `Dirichlet model`) |>
  kbl() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "left") |>
  footnote(general = "In the coral dominance model, benthic predictors and responses are coral dominance (log coral / fleshy algae); positive = more coral relative to algae. Dirichlet effects on coral and fleshy algae are on log(part / other cover).",
           general_title = "")
```

### Disturbance timing: current vs previous year

Coral surveys may precede the mortality caused by a disturbance in the same calendar year (e.g. bleaching late in the warm season), in which case losses would appear in the following year's survey. The dynamic coral equation is refit on its own with current-year disturbance, previous-year disturbance, or both. Because the annual block has no residual correlations, the coral equation alone gives the same posterior as within the block.

```{r sem-season-disturbance-lag}
#| label: sem-season-disturbance-lag
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["sem-season-preparation"]

coral_dist_data <- semdata_season |> filter(sub_coral)

coral_dist_forms <- list(
  current  = coraldom ~ 1 + coraldom_lag1 + temperature + Disturbance +
    logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1,
  previous = coraldom ~ 1 + coraldom_lag1 + temperature + Disturbance_lag1 +
    logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1,
  both     = coraldom ~ 1 + coraldom_lag1 + temperature + Disturbance +
    Disturbance_lag1 + logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1
)

coral_dist_fits <- lapply(coral_dist_forms, \(f) brm(
  f,
  data = coral_dist_data,
  prior = c(set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),
            set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept")),
  chains = 3,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  seed = 6081,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
))
```

```{r sem-season-disturbance-lag-compare}
#| label: sem-season-disturbance-lag-comparison

coral_dist_coefs <- map_dfr(names(coral_dist_fits), \(m) {
  fe <- fixef(coral_dist_fits[[m]])
  as_tibble(fe, rownames = "term") |>
    filter(term %in% c("coraldom_lag1", "Disturbance", "Disturbance_lag1")) |>
    mutate(model = m, .before = 1)
})
coral_dist_coefs |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

loo::loo_compare(lapply(coral_dist_fits, loo))
```

### Lagged coral dominance vs AR(1) residuals

The dynamic coral equation (previous-year coral dominance as a predictor) is compared with the earlier AR(1)-residual specification on the same rows and predictors. With AR(1) residuals, year-to-year memory sits in the error term, so a disturbance shifts coral dominance only in the year it occurs. With lagged coral dominance as a predictor, effects carry forward into later years. PSIS-LOO treats years as exchangeable, which is optimistic for time series; it is used here only for a like-for-like comparison of the two specifications.

```{r sem-season-ar-vs-lag}
#| label: sem-season-ar-vs-lag
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["sem-season-preparation", "sem-season-disturbance-lag"]

coral_ar_fit <- brm(
  coraldom ~ 1 + temperature + Disturbance + logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1 +
    ar(time = Year, p = 1),
  data = coral_dist_data,
  prior = c(set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),
            set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept"),
            set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "ar", lb = -1, ub = 1)),
  chains = 3,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  seed = 6081,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)
```

```{r sem-season-ar-vs-lag-compare}
#| label: sem-season-ar-vs-lag-comparison

coral_memory_fits <- list(lagged_coral = coral_dist_fits$current,
                          ar1_residual = coral_ar_fit)

loo::loo_compare(lapply(coral_memory_fits, loo))

tibble(
  model      = names(coral_memory_fits),
  R2         = sapply(coral_memory_fits, \(m) median(bayes_R2(m, summary = FALSE))),
  memory     = c(fixef(coral_dist_fits$current)["coraldom_lag1", "Estimate"],
                 posterior_summary(coral_ar_fit, variable = "ar[1]")[, "Estimate"]),
  temp       = sapply(coral_memory_fits, \(m) fixef(m)["temperature", "Estimate"]),
  disturbance = sapply(coral_memory_fits, \(m) fixef(m)["Disturbance", "Estimate"])
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

### Coral recruitment and the unexplained decline in coral dominance

Without recruitment, much of the 2007–2015 decline in coral dominance was not explained by the predictors. Because predictors are centred, the intercept of the dynamic equation is close to the sample-average change and changes little when a predictor is added. Whether recruitment explains the decline is therefore judged from the residuals: their SD, whether they are systematically negative during the decline (2007–2015) and positive afterwards, and their trend over time. The coral equation is compared with and without lagged recruitment on all 19 years (recruitment imputed for 2007, 2008 and 2021) and on the 16 years with observed recruitment (no imputation).

```{r sem-season-recruit-check}
#| label: sem-season-recruit-check
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["sem-season-preparation"]

rec_cc_data <- semdata_season |> filter(sub_coral, !is.na(logrec3))

fit_coral_eq <- function(f, data) {
  brm(f, data = data,
      prior = c(set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),
                set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept")),
      chains = 3, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000, seed = 6081,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), silent = 2, refresh = 0)
}

coral_base_form <- coraldom ~ 1 + coraldom_lag1 + temperature + Disturbance +
  logherbs_lag1 + logcoralliv_lag1

coral_rec_cc_fits <- list(
  without_recruitment = fit_coral_eq(coral_base_form, rec_cc_data),
  with_recruitment    = fit_coral_eq(update(coral_base_form, . ~ . + logrec3), rec_cc_data)
)
```

```{r sem-season-recruit-compare}
#| label: sem-season-recruit-comparison

coral_years_all <- as.numeric(as.character(semdata_season$year_f[semdata_season$sub_coral]))
coral_years_cc  <- as.numeric(as.character(rec_cc_data$year_f))

# Residual diagnostics (coral dominance SD units) from posterior mean fits
coral_resid_diag <- function(mu, y, years) {
  res <- y - colMeans(mu)
  var_mu <- apply(mu, 1, var)
  var_res <- apply(sweep(mu, 2, y), 1, var)
  tibble(
    n                      = length(y),
    R2                     = median(var_mu / (var_mu + var_res)),
    resid_sd               = sd(res),
    mean_resid_2007_2015   = mean(res[years <= 2015]),
    mean_resid_2016_2025   = mean(res[years > 2015]),
    resid_trend_per_decade = unname(coef(lm(res ~ years))[2]) * 10
  )
}

# Coefficient summary "est (lo, hi)" for a named term, NA if absent
coef_txt <- function(fe, term) {
  if (!term %in% rownames(fe)) return(NA_character_)
  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", fe[term, "Estimate"], fe[term, "Q2.5"], fe[term, "Q97.5"])
}

fe_main <- fixef(brms_sem_season_annual_cd)
fe_dist <- fixef(coral_dist_fits$current)
fe_cc0  <- fixef(coral_rec_cc_fits$without_recruitment)
fe_cc1  <- fixef(coral_rec_cc_fits$with_recruitment)

coral_recruit_diag <- bind_rows(
  coral_resid_diag(posterior_epred(coral_dist_fits$current), coral_dist_data$coraldom,
                   coral_years_all) |>
    mutate(model = "19 yr, without recruitment",
           phi = coef_txt(fe_dist, "coraldom_lag1"),
           recruitment = NA_character_,
           intercept = coef_txt(fe_dist, "Intercept")),
  coral_resid_diag(posterior_epred(brms_sem_season_annual_cd, resp = "coraldom"),
                   semdata_season$coraldom[semdata_season$sub_coral], coral_years_all) |>
    mutate(model = "19 yr, with recruitment (imputed; coral dominance SEM)",
           phi = coef_txt(fe_main, "coraldom_coraldom_lag1"),
           recruitment = coef_txt(fe_main, "coraldom_milogrec3idxEQobs_id"),
           intercept = coef_txt(fe_main, "coraldom_Intercept")),
  coral_resid_diag(posterior_epred(coral_rec_cc_fits$without_recruitment),
                   rec_cc_data$coraldom, coral_years_cc) |>
    mutate(model = "16 yr, without recruitment",
           phi = coef_txt(fe_cc0, "coraldom_lag1"),
           recruitment = NA_character_,
           intercept = coef_txt(fe_cc0, "Intercept")),
  coral_resid_diag(posterior_epred(coral_rec_cc_fits$with_recruitment),
                   rec_cc_data$coraldom, coral_years_cc) |>
    mutate(model = "16 yr, with recruitment (observed only)",
           phi = coef_txt(fe_cc1, "coraldom_lag1"),
           recruitment = coef_txt(fe_cc1, "logrec3"),
           intercept = coef_txt(fe_cc1, "Intercept"))
) |>
  select(model, n, recruitment, phi, intercept, R2, resid_sd,
         mean_resid_2007_2015, mean_resid_2016_2025, resid_trend_per_decade)

coral_recruit_diag |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

# Level the dynamic coral equation relaxes towards: intercept / (1 - phi),
# using draws with phi < 1 (stationary)
coral_eq_draws <- as_draws_df(brms_sem_season_annual_cd) |>
  filter(b_coraldom_coraldom_lag1 < 1) |>
  mutate(equilibrium = b_coraldom_Intercept / (1 - b_coraldom_coraldom_lag1))
coral_equilibrium <- quantile(coral_eq_draws$equilibrium, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
coral_equilibrium

# Out-of-sample comparison on the same rows
recruit_loo_all <- loo::loo_compare(list(
  without_recruitment = loo(coral_dist_fits$current),
  with_recruitment    = loo_block(brms_sem_season_annual_cd, resp = "coraldom")
))
recruit_loo_cc <- loo::loo_compare(lapply(coral_rec_cc_fits, loo))
recruit_loo_all
recruit_loo_cc
```

Lagged lagoon recruitment had a coefficient of `r coral_recruit_diag$recruitment[2]` in the coral dominance SEM (imputed years included) and `r coral_recruit_diag$recruitment[4]` using observed years only. Adding it changed the residual SD of coral dominance from `r fmt(coral_recruit_diag$resid_sd[1])` to `r fmt(coral_recruit_diag$resid_sd[2])` SD, and the PSIS-LOO difference was `r fmt(abs(recruit_loo_all[2, "elpd_diff"]), 1)` ± `r fmt(recruit_loo_all[2, "se_diff"], 1)` (all years) and `r fmt(abs(recruit_loo_cc[2, "elpd_diff"]), 1)` ± `r fmt(recruit_loo_cc[2, "se_diff"], 1)` (observed years). Even without recruitment, residuals were close to zero on average during the decline (2007–2015: `r fmt(coral_recruit_diag$mean_resid_2007_2015[1])`) and afterwards (2016–2025: `r fmt(coral_recruit_diag$mean_resid_2016_2025[1])`). The dynamic equation reproduces the decline as relaxation towards a low equilibrium coral dominance of `r fmt(coral_equilibrium[2])` SD (95% CI `r fmt(coral_equilibrium[1])`, `r fmt(coral_equilibrium[3])`; observed range `r fmt(min(semdata_season$coraldom[semdata_season$sub_coral]))` to `r fmt(max(semdata_season$coraldom[semdata_season$sub_coral]))`). The covariates, including recruitment, explain little of the year-to-year deviation from that path. What remains unexplained is why coral dominance started far above this equilibrium in 2006, and what set the equilibrium so low.

## Software and Reproducibility

Key packages: **tidyverse** 2.0 (Wickham et al. 2019), **brms** 2.21 (Bürkner 2017), **tidybayes** 3.0 (Kay 2023), **patchwork** 1.2 (Pedersen 2024), **ggraph** 2.1 and **igraph** 1.6 (Csárdi & Nepusz 2006), **httr2** (Wickham 2023), **zoo** (Zeileis & Grothendieck 2005), **cowplot** (Wilke 2024), **ecmwfr** (Hufkens et al. 2019; https://bluegreen-labs.github.io/ecmwfr/), **ncdf4** (Pierce 2024). Stan 2.32 served as the computational backend. CMIP6 SST data were accessed from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/projections-cmip6; DOI: 10.24381/cds.c866074c). MCR LTER raw data are publicly archived through the EDI Data Portal (https://edirepository.org).
